config.title: Loyalty Points, Brainstorm 1
config.tagline: Points at checkout, looked at through six hats

topic.title: Loyalty points at checkout
topic.question: Should checkout offer loyalty points?
topic.context: The checkout redesign kept guest checkout, and the CRM team still wants a reason for guests to make an account. Points are the idea on the table. Nothing is built yet, so this is the time to look at it from every side.

detail.text: 41% of completed purchases came through guest checkout.
Guest orders are unreachable for lifecycle marketing.

hats.line: Today's focus is points at checkout. Five hats, then back to me.
Numbers first. Here is what we have, and what nobody has measured.
hats.question: What do we know about points at checkout?

ideas.text: 41% of purchases come through guest checkout, and guests can't hold points.
Nobody has asked shoppers whether they would join.
ideas.why: No survey or test covers it.

ideas.text: Both launch payment providers can show a points balance.
Last year's coupon test lifted repeat orders for two months, then faded.
ideas.why: From last year's coupon test results.

hats.ask: What do you know about our shoppers that I don't?

hats.line: Never mind the numbers. How does it feel?
hats.question: How does points at checkout feel?

ideas.text: Points feel like a thank-you.
Another box at checkout feels like a hurdle.
Shoppers are tired of joining loyalty programs.

hats.ask: What does your gut say about points?

hats.line: Let's see what's good about it.
hats.question: What could points at checkout do for us?

ideas.text: Points give guests a reason to make an account after paying.
Repeat buyers get something back, so they come back sooner.
A points balance gives the CRM team a reason to write.

hats.line: Someone has to look for the cracks.
hats.question: What could go wrong with points at checkout?

ideas.text: A points line adds weight to the page with the biggest drop-off.
ideas.why: Checkout loses more shoppers than any other page.

ideas.text: Unspent points sit on the books as money owed.
ideas.why: Points count as a debt until they are spent or expire.

ideas.text: Points that take months to add up feel like nothing.
ideas.why: Most shoppers order only a few times a year.

hats.line: What if we did something else entirely?
hats.question: What else could we try?

ideas.text: Show the points, don't ask: "This order earns 120 points", with Join after payment.
Free shipping over a threshold instead of points.
Points only from the second order.
Let guests claim their points by email within 30 days.

hats.line: Here is what you starred. Now, what's next?
hats.question: What did we find, and what should happen next?

ideas.text: Ask 200 shoppers whether they would join, before building anything.
Decide where the points line sits: before or after payment.
Price unspent points with finance.
